built_from: ../../sources/limits-of-observability.data.json (the hub rows the asks link to)
caveats: core-et in external/ is the Erbium branch; external/core-et-main is Ainekko's re-implementation of the CORE-ET RTL, co-simulated against the original shire cache.
The Shire Cache Specification is v1.1 and also describes later chips (Nemi, Gepardo).

l1:l1.size.statement: Each minion has a private 4 KB L1 data cache: 16 sets x 4 ways x 64-byte lines (set = PA[9:6]).
l1:l1.size.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.9 (§2.1.1.5, text L341-345); external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29 (§3.2, text L1266); external/core-et/rtl/inc/minion_defines.vh:125,143 (DCACHE_SETS 16, DCACHE_WAYS 4); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:27 (line 64 B)

l1:l1.lram.statement: The data array is not SRAM: it is built from latch RAM, "4 LRAM (Latch-RAM) blocks of 128 rows and 64 bits per row", each block with a single read port and a single write port.
l1:l1.lram.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29 (§3.2, text L1269-1271) and glossary pdf p.61 ("LRAM Latch Random Access Memory"); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.9 (§2.1.1.5, text L346)
l1:l1.lram.note: Answers the lab lead's "not SRAM" for the L1: latch RAM. Both the design doc and the public datasheet say so.

l1:l1.lram-macros.statement: In the RTL each 128 x 64 block is a wrapper of two 128 x 32 one-read-one-write LRAM macros (low and high 32-bit halves) with their own read and write enables: 8 macros (dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram) per minion.
l1:l1.lram-macros.unit: macros of 128 x 32 bit per minion

l1:l1.lram-model.statement: The released LRAM macro is only a behavioural model ("One-read, one-write register file ... synchronous write, synchronous read"); the cell-level design of the silicon macro is not in the open release.
l1:l1.lram-model.note: See unknown l1.u-cell. The port list (clk, rd/wr enable, 7-bit rd/wr address, 32-bit data) is all the model fixes.

l1:l1.latch-rf.statement: The ET latch register-file library ("Latch based Register Files with registered read output") shows the write and read mechanism these arrays use: write data is captured by a low-phase latch clocked by a negative clock gate one phase before the write; the decoded write address enables one per-row clock gate; that row's latches are transparent while its gated clock is high; the read address is registered on the rising edge and the read is a combinational select rf[rd_addr_reg] (no bitline, no sense amplifier in the model).
l1:l1.latch-rf.source: external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/rf_latch_1r_1w_reg.v:4-52 (timing diagram and notes), 88-96 (write-data latch), 101-136 (per-row clock gates and latches), 139-149 (registered read address, combinational read)
l1:l1.latch-rf.note: core-et-main maps the D-cache LRAM wrappers to exactly this contract, "preview-plus-registered-read RF" (external/core-et-main/docs/latch_translation.md:55-56, 93-96; external/core-et-main/hw/ip/minion/dcache/rtl/minion_dcache_128x64_1r1w_lram.sv:35-63). Whether the silicon macro is this library cell-for-cell is unknown (l1.u-cell).

l1:l1.icg-cells.statement: The clock gates of the latch arrays are standard cells when the ASIC cell switch is on: HDBULT08_CKGTPLT_V7Y2_2 (rising-edge gate, per row) and HDBULT08_CKGTNLT_V5Y2_2 (falling-edge gate, write-data latch). Other cells named in the RTL come from HDBULT08_* and HDBULT11_* families.
l1:l1.icg-cells.source: external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/et_clk_gate.v:14-18; external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/et_clk_gate_n.v:14-18; external/core-et/rtl/inc/libs_defines.vh:8-9 (switch off in the open release: "Standard cells not available")
l1:l1.icg-cells.note: Library vendor, track height and threshold flavour are not stated (l1.u-library).

l1:l1.lram-addr.statement: LRAM row address = {set[3:0], half-line bit, way[1:0]} = {addr[9:5], way[1:0]}: 7 bits, 128 rows. Address bits [4:3] choose the block (8 bytes each); one row across the 4 blocks is 32 bytes, half a line; a 64-byte line occupies 2 rows, and the 4 ways of a half-line sit in 4 adjacent rows.
l1:l1.lram-addr.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29-30 (§3.2, text L1276-1296, Figure 10); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.10 (Figure 2-3); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_data_array.v:46-50

l1:l1.bank-enables.statement: Only the blocks a load needs are read: a scalar load enables the one block whose addr[4:3] matches (both of its 32-bit halves); a 32-byte packed-single (PS) vector load enables all four; a misaligned access also reads the next row in the following blocks.
l1:l1.bank-enables.source: external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:2123-2147; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.10 (text L352-361, worked examples)
l1:l1.bank-enables.note: A 4-byte flw still reads the whole 64-bit block row: valid_h = valid_l (dcache_top.v:2141; the RTL comment at :2459 reads "OPTIMIZE, check if it can be split").

l1:l1.phased.statement: Tag first, then data: in S1 the physical tag is compared with all 4 ways (four comparators) and the hit way is encoded; the S2 data read then reads only that way's row, because the way is part of the LRAM row address.
l1:l1.phased.source: external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:2108-2121 ("CAM for the tags"), 2145; external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_data_array.v:49-50; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.24-25 (§3.1.2-3.1.3)
l1:l1.phased.note: GENERIC: a serial tag-then-data cache reads one way instead of four, at the cost of a pipeline stage.

l1:l1.metadata.statement: Metadata: 64 entries (16 sets x 4 ways) of tag PA[39:7] (33 bits) + 2-bit line state = 35 bits, held in four latch register files (one per way, 16 entries, read in the same cycle); the 64 valid bits are flip-flops.
l1:l1.metadata.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.31 (§3.3, text L1350-1361) and pdf p.57 (§3.12.1, text L2457-2458); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_metadata_array.v:39-65 (rf_latch_1r_1w per way, valid in RST_EN_FF); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_types.vh:183-187; external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/rf_latch_1r_1w.v:49-50 ("read latency = 0")

l1:l1.states.statement: Line states: invalid 00, shared 01 (never assigned: there is no coherence at this level), exclusive 10 (after a fill for a read), modified 11 (after a fill for a write, or a store to a clean line).
l1:l1.states.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.31 (text L1359-1361) and pdf p.35 (text L1491-1509)

l1:l1.noncoherent.statement: The L1 data caches are not coherent: software moves lines with cache operations (EvictVA, FlushVA, PrefetchVA, lock/unlock) and fences.
l1:l1.noncoherent.source: external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.1 (text L7 "Non-coherent"); external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.31 (text L1361); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.243-244 (§8.1, text L5872-5923)

l1:l1.write-policy.statement: Write-back, write-allocate: a cacheable store that misses fetches the line (miss handler fill) and marks it modified; a dirty victim is evicted to the L2 as 512 bits in two 256-bit transfers, reading the LRAM 256 bits a cycle.
l1:l1.write-policy.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.21 (text L776-781), pdf p.33 (§3.5, text L1404-1407), pdf p.35 (text L1491-1509)

l1:l1.store-rmw.statement: Every store is a read-modify-write of the array: the row is read in S2, the new bytes are aligned and merged in S3, and the merged row is written through the write port in S4.
l1:l1.store-rmw.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.25 (text L955-957), pdf p.27 (§3.1.5, text L1116-1129)

l1:l1.lru.statement: Replacement is LRU: 16 bits per set (a 4 x 4 order matrix), in flip-flops, updated in S2 on every cacheable access; hard- and soft-locked ways are excluded when choosing the victim.
l1:l1.lru.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:31; external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_lru_array.v (RST_EN_FF per set); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:2722-2744, 3150-3159; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.25 (text L954)

l1:l1.pipeline.statement: Six DCache stages, locked to the integer pipeline: pre-S0 = ID (arbitration bids), S0 = EX (address, grant), S1 = TAG (TLB, metadata read, tag match, PMA, data-array address), S2 = MEM (data-array read, hit/miss, replay queue, miss handler), S3 = WB (align, sign-extend, return to core or VPU), S4 (data-array write port), S5 (store data bypass to S3).
l1:l1.pipeline.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.22 (Figure 3), pdf p.23-28 (§3.1.1-3.1.6); external/core-et/docs/FE-Intpipe-Description.pdf, pdf p.9 (§3.1, text L201-212), pdf p.12 (text L224-227)

l1:l1.s0-arb.statement: Pre-S0 priority, high to low: cache-ops metadata read, debug, write-back unit (reads the data array), replay queue, cache-ops L1 prefetch, core intpipe. The VPU scratchpad read, Reduce, TensorLoad and cache-op prefetch can also take S0.
l1:l1.s0-arb.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.24 (§3.1.1, text L839-857)

l1:l1.s4-arb.statement: One write port per block, static priority: stores in S4, fills from the SEND port, L2 fills from the miss handlers, TensorLoad transformation writes, configuration clear, cache-ops clear, debug. A fill may write only if there is no store and the read port was not granted in the previous cycle.
l1:l1.s4-arb.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.27 (§3.1.5, text L1116-1129)

l1:l1.mh.statement: Two miss handlers per minion (DCACHE_MH_FILE_SIZE = 2, the only verified value): at most two outstanding cacheable line misses; a later access to a line already being filled joins the same handler.
l1:l1.mh.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.34-35 (§3.6, text L1449-1480); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:79

l1:l1.rq.statement: Replay queue of 8 entries, pre-allocated at ID; a missing or rejected instruction waits there and re-enters the pipeline; when it is full the core is told id_core_ready = 0.
l1:l1.rq.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.38 (§3.7, text L1634-1649); external/core-et/rtl/inc/minion_defines.vh:151

l1:l1.tlb.statement: An 8-entry TLB (a latch register file) translates in S1 (4 KB, 2 MB and 1 GB pages); the neighbourhood document notes that "Virtual Memory logic is unused in A0".
l1:l1.tlb.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:105; external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/tlb_top.v:277-285; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.15 (§2.4.1); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.6 (footnote 1, text L143)
l1:l1.tlb.note: workloads/memprobe/README.md treats kernel addresses as physical ("offset bits are physical address bits").

l1:l1.vpu-port.statement: The array feeds one 256-bit register-file entry of all 8 VPU lanes per cycle (DCACHE_DATA_SIZE 256).

l1:l1.vpu-scp-read.statement: The VPU reads the scratchpad directly: its request in S1 pre-empts any other S1 operation (sent to the replay queue), no tag check is made, and the 256 bits are delivered in S3, two cycles later (one extra register stage for timing).
l1:l1.vpu-scp-read.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.12-13 (§2.3, §2.3.1, text L416-451, Figure 1)

l1:l1.modes.statement: Three modes (mcache_control D1Split, ScpEnable): shared (both harts, all 16 sets); split (hart 0 sets 0-7, hart 1 sets 14-15, sets 8-13 unused); scratchpad (hart 0 sets 12-13, hart 1 sets 14-15, sets 0-11 = 48 lines = 3 KB of tensor scratchpad, hart 0 only).
l1:l1.modes.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.245-246 (§8.3.1, Table 8.4, text L5977-6010); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:130 (DCACHE_TL_SCP_MAX_IDX 48)
l1:l1.modes.note: The Minion Overview slide draws split mode as 2 KB per hart; the PRM table is followed here.

l1:l1.scp-impl.statement: Scratchpad mode is implemented in the same array: two more tag bits are kept and the two set MSBs are forced to 11, so the cache uses only sets 12-15; changing ScpEnable drains the pipeline, writes zeros into every line of sets 0-13 and invalidates their metadata.
l1:l1.scp-impl.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.30-31 (§3.2.1, text L1318-1347); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.246 (text L6012-6019); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_metadata_array.v:92-108 (cfg_clear_low)

l1:l1.firmware-mode.statement: The firmware sets D1Split and ScpEnable before every launch, so a kernel runs with 512 B of L1 cache per hart (2 sets x 4 ways x 64 B) and a 3 KB scratchpad.

l1:l1.knee.statement: The measured knee confirms 512 B per hart: hart 1 reads 5.25 cycles at 256 B, 5.256 at 512 B and 39.0 at 768 B (a miss to the L2 read buffer), in every pass on three cards.

l1:l1.tensorload.statement: TensorLoad (unit TL0) writes L2 responses straight into scratchpad rows through the write port; TensorLoadB (TL1) skips the array and fills a 4-entry VPU buffer under 4 (up to 6) credits; up to 4 L2 transfers are in flight; transposes and interleaves stage through a 128-byte buffer and write the LRAM in 8-byte chunks.
l1:l1.tensorload.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.15 (§2.3.4), pdf p.40-43 (§3.9.1-3.9.2); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:108

l1:l1.tl-latency.statement: One minion's TensorLoad into its L1 scratchpad: 16 lines (1 KB) take 160.4 cycles from the L2 and 160.1 from the own scratchpad; 8 lines 80.1; 4 lines 41.9 cycles; the same on three cards.

l1:l1.tl-rate.statement: About 10 cycles per 64-byte line into the scratchpad (6.4 B per cycle): what 4 transfers in flight over a round trip of about 40 cycles allow.
l1:l1.tl-rate.source: derived from docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/lat.json LAT-S2 (160.4 / 80.1 / 41.9 cycles for 16 / 8 / 4 lines) and external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:108
l1:l1.tl-rate.note: Little's law with the RTL constant; the round trip itself is not separately measured.

l1:l1.lv-region.statement: The eight minions of a neighbourhood sit in its low-voltage (LV) region with their own clock; the neighbourhood says the memory cells of its ICache data RAMs "need to be placed in an HV region", so those RAMs were moved out into the shire channel.
l1:l1.lv-region.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.6 (§2, text L108-112), pdf p.7 (§2.2, text L150-154), pdf p.14 (§4.2, text L511-518)

l1:l1.why-latch.statement: Why latches: the data cache sits inside the minion, in the neighbourhood's LV region. The neighbourhood document says that "the memory cells used to implement the ICache data RAMs need to be placed in an HV region"; that the same holds for the shire cache's SRAM panels, and that the data cache is a latch array because latches are ordinary logic that runs on the minion supply, is our inference.
l1:l1.why-latch.source: combines l1.lram (external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf pdf p.29) and l1.lv-region (external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf pdf p.14 §4.2); minion-rail limits docs/research/power-telemetry.md:189-190 (bl2_pmic_controller.h:165-244); Vmin external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.51 Tables 13-14
l1:l1.why-latch.note: The documents never state this rationale for the data cache (asked). A voltage argument is consistent with it but does not prove it, and it is about the listed Vmin of these macros only: the firmware limits the minion rail to 400-620 mV (400 mV nominal), while the 1PUHD data panels list 585 mV as their lowest Vmin (RM0) and the 2PUHDRF tag-state RAM 540 mV (Shire Cache Specification pdf p.51 Tables 13-14).

l1:l1.icache-sram.statement: Contrast at the same level: the neighbourhood's instruction-cache data RAM (mbi) is 'saduls0g4l1p512x144m4b1...', the same 1PUHD macro family as the shire cache's data panels, which the spec calls 'SRAM memory panels'; the PRM calls the SADULS family SRAMs, and the neighbourhood document says its memory cells must sit in an HV region. Its bitcell is as unknown as the shire cache's.
l1:l1.icache-sram.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.51 Table 14 (icache_ram (mbi)), pdf p.48 §2.14.5; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.346 ('Configuration bits for SADULS SRAM's'); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf pdf p.14 §4.2
l1:l1.icache-sram.note: external/core-et/rtl/libs/macros/icache_data_ram.v calls it a '512 x 144-bit synchronous SRAM', but that file is a behavioural stand-in (Ainekko, 2026), like the L1's dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram.v, and says nothing about the cell.

l1:l1.rail.statement: The L1 is powered from the minion rail (VDD_MNN), not the SRAM rail (VDD_SRAM, the shire-cache arrays): an L1-hit loop puts 83% of its power over idle on the minion rail and 2% on the SRAM rail; on 19 September an 8-byte ld L1 hit cost 40.7 pJ on the minion rail and 1.3 pJ on the SRAM rail.
l1:l1.rail.source: docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md:168; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/power/summary.json: summary.l1.pj_per_load (minion 40.74, sram 1.33, noc 0.56, board 56.47); docs/research/power-telemetry.md:14, 44, 46

l1:l1.voltage.statement: The latch arrays switch at the minion-rail voltage: 0.517 V at 600 MHz (0.568 V at 700, 0.618 V at 800). The card's power tree gives the minion rail 400 mV nominal, and the firmware limits it to 400-620 mV.

l1:l1.no-sleep.statement: The minion's sleep and isolation ports (nsleepin, iso_enable, nsleepout) are marked "not used", and no firmware drives them: the L1 arrays are always powered, with no retention or wake-up state.
l1:l1.no-sleep.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion Description.pdf, pdf p.7 (text L126-133); docs/findings/16-dvfs-and-leakage.md:23

l1:l1.no-parity.statement: No parity or ECC appears in the open data-cache RTL: each LRAM row is 64 data bits (core-et-main's 128 x 72 variant is instantiated nowhere).
l1:l1.no-parity.note: Absence in the open RTL; the silicon is not confirmed (l1.u-parity).

l1:l1.bits.statement: Storage per minion: 32,768 data bits in latch RAM, 2,240 tag and state bits in latch register files, 64 valid and 256 LRU flip-flops. Over 1,088 minions that is 35.7 Mbit (4.25 MB) of latch-RAM data.

l1:l1.transistors.statement: Estimate: at 8-12 transistors per latch bit, the data array holds about 0.26-0.39 million storage transistors per minion (0.29-0.43 billion on the chip, 1.2-1.8% of its >24 billion), against 0.2 million for the same 4 KB in 6T SRAM.
l1:l1.transistors.source: l1.bits x GENERIC transistors per bit; chip total from docs/findings/01-resources.md:101
l1:l1.transistors.note: GENERIC count per bit; the real latch cell is unknown (l1.u-cell). Excludes decoders, clock gates and read muxes.

l1:l1.latency.statement: L1 hit: 5.25 cycles load-to-use in a dependent pointer chase (8.75 ns at 600 MHz), per-pass ranges 5.247-5.259, in every pass on three cards.

l1:l1.latency-5.statement: A dependent L1 load issues 5 cycles after the previous one: ID, EX, TAG, MEM, WB (data leaves S3 at WB) and the next ID. The 0.25 cycle in 5.25 fits 2 cycles of loop overhead per 8 unrolled loads; the anatomy page sets an L1 hit to 5 cycles.
l1:l1.latency-5.source: external/core-et/docs/FE-Intpipe-Description.pdf, pdf p.9 (text L201-208), pdf p.12 (text L234-235: "DCache data is available at the WB stage or later"); workloads/memhier/kernel/memhier.c:36-44; workloads/memprobe/README.md ("offset chosen so an L1 hit reads the 5 cycles")
l1:l1.latency-5.note: Stage-by-stage timing is inferred from the documents; no probe times a single stage (l1.u-cycles).

l1:l1.miss-l2.statement: When the load misses the L1: 36 cycles if the line is in the L2 read buffer, 47 if it is in the L2 or the own scratchpad; hart 1 pays 3 more (39 and 50).
l1:l1.miss-l2.note: The L1's own share of these cycles (miss detection, miss handler, fill write, replay) is not measured apart.

l1:l1.bw.statement: L1 bandwidth: 14.5 TB/s over the chip with 32-byte vector loads on both harts (23.6 B per minion-cycle of the 32 designed); 6.2 TB/s in the memory-hierarchy probe's loop.

l1:l1.e-vload.statement: One 32-byte vector load (flw.ps) that hits the L1: 0.54 pJ/B on random data [0.52-0.56] = 17.3 pJ per load (aifoundry2 17.6, aifoundry3 17.3, aifoundry1-c1 16.6); 0.39 pJ/B on zeros = 12.5 pJ per load. Above idle, including the instruction.

l1:l1.e-vstore.statement: One 32-byte vector store (fsw.ps) that hits the L1: 0.72 pJ/B on random data [0.66-0.81] = 23.0 pJ per store (aifoundry2 23.4, aifoundry3 23.0, aifoundry1-c1 22.7); 0.41 pJ/B on zeros = 13.1 pJ.

l1:l1.e-scalar.statement: Scalar 4-byte accesses that hit the L1 (512 B table per hart, all 1,024 minions): flw 14.0 pJ [13.4-14.5], fsw 25.5 pJ [24.8-26.4]; the 8-lane gather fgw.ps 12.8 pJ and scatter fscw.ps 14.7 pJ per element.

l1:l1.e-store-ratio.statement: A store costs more than a load of the same size: 1.82x for scalar (25.5 / 14.0 pJ), 1.33x for 32-byte vectors (0.72 / 0.54 pJ/B), consistent with the store touching the array twice (S2 read, S4 write).

l1:l1.e-memhier.statement: L1 hits in the memory-hierarchy loop: 0.75 pJ/B [0.62-0.88] = 24.0 pJ per 32-byte load (aifoundry2 0.77, aifoundry3 0.75, aifoundry1-c1 0.72 pJ/B); the manual recommends the 0.54 figure.

l1:l1.e-rails.statement: Split by rail on three cards (the energy manual's catalogue, 26 September): both harts of every minion re-reading the L1 with 32-byte vector loads (flw.ps, random data) put 80, 82 and 87% of the power above idle on the minion rail, 2% on the SRAM rail, 1% or less on the mesh and 17, 15 and 9% on no metered rail (aifoundry2, aifoundry3 and aifoundry1 card 1). An L1 hit is the minion rail's.
l1:l1.e-rails.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.cards.<card>.summary['flw.ps/random/h2'] (rails_over_w, over_idle_w), as Anatomy of a memory access §6 splits it (workloads/memprobe/build_report.py)
l1:l1.e-rails.note: Until 28 September this row gave the first measurement, on 19 September on aifoundry2 alone (an 8-byte ld hitting the L1 in a power loop; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/power/summary.json summary.l1); Anatomy of a memory access keeps those runs as one note, and its §6 shows this split.

l1:l1.e-fill.statement: Filling one 64-byte line from the own scratchpad into the L1: 238 pJ on random data (aifoundry2 221, aifoundry3 223, aifoundry1-c1 271), 101 pJ on zeros; random data adds 269 fJ per bit on the path into the L1.
l1:l1.e-fill.note: Difference of two measured stride rows, times 2.

l1:l1.e-per-bit.statement: Per bit delivered, a 32-byte L1 load costs at most 68 fJ on random data and 49 fJ on zeros, of which random data adds 4.8 pJ per load, 19 fJ per bit; these bound the array from above (they include issue, pipeline and register write).

l1:g.latch-cell.statement: A static CMOS D-latch (transmission-gate or clocked-inverter type) stores a bit on a pair of cross-coupled inverters with a clocked feedback path: about 8-12 transistors per bit, full-swing, no precharge, no sense amplifier, readable without disturbing the stored value.

l1:g.latch-read.statement: A latch-array read is logic: the registered address drives a decoder or a mux tree (128:1 per output bit, e.g. seven 2:1 levels or four 4:1 levels), and only the nodes whose value changes spend energy, so read energy depends on the data.

l1:g.latch-write.statement: A latch-array write: the write-address decoder enables one row's integrated clock gate (a latch plus an AND, about 10-16 transistors); its gated clock goes high and every latch in that row becomes transparent and takes the write bus, which an opposite-phase latch holds steady for the whole phase.
l1:g.latch-write.source: textbook latch register-file design (GENERIC); the opposite-phase write latch and per-row gates are the ET pattern in l1.latch-rf

l1:g.sram-6t.statement: For contrast, a 6T SRAM cell: two cross-coupled inverters (4 transistors) and two NMOS access transistors on complementary bitlines. A read precharges the bitlines, the wordline driver raises one wordline, one bitline droops by a fraction of VDD and a sense amplifier resolves it through a column mux; the cell needs a minimum voltage for read stability and writability, which is why SRAM usually gets its own higher rail.

l1:g.compare.statement: A tag comparator is one XNOR per bit (about 8-12 transistors) and an AND tree over the 33 bits; four run on every access, hit or miss.
l1:g.compare.source: textbook logic (GENERIC); four comparators and 33-bit tags from l1.phased, l1.metadata

l1:g.flipflop.statement: The valid and LRU bits are edge-triggered flip-flops: two latches in master-slave, about 20-24 transistors each.

l1:g.no-refresh.statement: Latches, like SRAM, hold data statically while powered: the L1 needs no refresh (unlike the DRAM level).

l1:l1.u-cell.statement: What is inside the dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram macro on silicon: standard-cell latches placed like the rf_latch_1r_1w_reg library, or a custom or compiled latch-array macro? Which latch cell (transistors per bit), and is the read a static mux tree or a precharged read bitline with a keeper or sense stage?
l1:l1.u-cell.note: Settles: the transistor-level panel of the L1 diagram, now drawn from the generic latch-RF template (l1.latch-rf, g.latch-cell, g.latch-read): cell topology, read path, and the transistor estimate l1.transistors.

l1:l1.u-why.statement: Is the data cache latch RAM because the minion sits in the neighbourhood's low-voltage region, where SRAM cells cannot be placed? Which other in-minion arrays are latch RAM or register files (VPU register file vpu_64x32_3r2w, tag arrays, TLB) and which, if any, are SRAM?
l1:l1.u-why.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf pdf p.29; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf pdf p.14 (the reason is our inference, l1.why-latch)
l1:l1.u-why.note: Settles: the "latch RAM, not SRAM, because ..." caption on the L1 page and which blocks the diagram draws as latch arrays.

l1:l1.u-library.statement: What are the HDBULT08 and HDBULT11 standard-cell families (vendor, track height, threshold voltage), and what is the "MMI (hand-tuned)" logic in the Minion Overview slides: does it include the LRAM or the tag compare?
l1:l1.u-library.source: external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/et_clk_gate.v:17; external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.1-2 (text L22, L44)
l1:l1.u-library.note: Settles: the cell names and drawing style on the circuit panel, and whether the L1 is drawn as hand-placed custom logic.

l1:l1.u-energy.statement: What are the post-layout energies of the LRAM at 0.52 V: pJ per 64-bit read, per 64-bit write, per tag lookup (4 ways), and leakage per macro?
l1:l1.u-energy.note: Settles: splitting the measured 12.5-17.3 pJ per 32-byte load (l1.e-vload) into array, tag check, pipeline and register write on the diagram's energy bars, instead of one bar for the whole load.

l1:l1.u-floorplan.statement: Where do the 8 LRAM macros, the tag register files and the TLB sit in the minion's physical partition, and how large are they (area of the 4 KB array against the minion)?
l1:l1.u-floorplan.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.7 (§2.2: minions are an independent physical partition; no minion floorplan)
l1:l1.u-floorplan.note: Settles: the physical layer of the L1 diagram: where the arrays light up inside the minion tile.

l1:l1.u-cycles.statement: Is the 5-cycle load-to-use of an L1 hit ID -> EX -> TAG -> MEM -> WB plus one cycle to the dependent's ID, with no bypass from S3 into EX? What costs hart 1 three extra cycles on every L1 miss?
l1:l1.u-cycles.note: Settles: the per-stage timeline annotations of the load-hit animation, and a hart-1 note on the miss path.

l1:l1.u-parity.statement: Does the taped-out L1 carry parity or ECC, and can the minion arrays be put to sleep or retention on silicon?
l1:l1.u-parity.note: Settles: whether the diagram shows check bits per row and sleep transistors on the arrays (the open RTL shows neither).

l1:l1.seq.load-hit.1.statement: cycle 0, intpipe ID = DCache pre-S0: integer pipeline ID stage; DCache replay queue; pre-S0 arbiter. Reads the base register, checks the scoreboard, pre-allocates a replay-queue entry and bids for the DCache (the core is the lowest of six bidders).
l1:l1.seq.load-hit.1.source: external/core-et/docs/FE-Intpipe-Description.pdf, pdf p.12 (§3.2.1); external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.23-24 (§3.1.1), pdf p.38 (text L1647-1649)

l1:l1.seq.load-hit.2.statement: cycle 1, EX = S0: ALU; S0 request mux. Adds base + offset into the virtual address; the granted request (address, destination register, command, size) is registered into S1.
l1:l1.seq.load-hit.2.source: external/core-et/docs/FE-Intpipe-Description.pdf, pdf p.13 (text L276-281); external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.23 (text L796-799)

l1:l1.seq.load-hit.3.statement: cycle 2, TAG = S1: TLB (8-entry latch RF); metadata array (4 tag latch RFs + valid flip-flops); 4 tag comparators; PMA; LRU read. Set = PA[9:6] with the mode's forced MSBs; each of the 4 way-RFs puts out its 35-bit entry for that set in the same cycle; four 33-bit comparisons give a one-hot hit, encoded to the way; the PMA checks cacheability; the data-array row address {set, half, way} and the one block enable (addr[4:3]) are formed and captured by the LRAM's read-address register at the clock edge.
l1:l1.seq.load-hit.3.source: external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:2108-2147; external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_metadata_array.v:55-80, 114-119; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.24-25 (§3.1.2, Figure 5)

l1:l1.seq.load-hit.4.statement: cycle 3, MEM = S2: data array: 1 of 4 blocks = 2 macros of 128 x 32 (LRAM); hit logic; LRU flip-flops. In the enabled block the 7-bit row address selects the hit way's row; its 64 latches drive the read select to the 64-bit output, which is registered into the S2->S3 data registers; the other 3 blocks stay idle. The hit is confirmed and the set's LRU matrix is rewritten.
l1:l1.seq.load-hit.4.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.25 (§3.1.3, text L930-957); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_data_array.v:66-75, 119-136; external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:3150-3159

l1:l1.seq.load-hit.5.statement: cycle 4, WB = S3: byte aligner, sign/zero extension, store bypass; integer register file. Picks the 8 bytes out of the data registers, sign- or zero-extends, merges data from older stores still in S4/S5, and returns the value on s3_core_resp; the integer register file is written in WB.
l1:l1.seq.load-hit.5.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.26 (§3.1.4, text L1016-1027); external/core-et/docs/FE-Intpipe-Description.pdf, pdf p.15 (§3.2.6)

l1:l1.seq.load-hit.6.statement: cycle 5, next ID: dependent instruction. A dependent load can read the value: 5 cycles issue to issue, measured as 5.25 in the unrolled chase on three cards; about 17 pJ per 32-byte load above idle on random data, including the instruction.

l1:l1.seq.store-hit.1.statement: ID to S1: as a load. Address, tag lookup and hit way exactly as a load; the store data is sent in the TAG stage (S1) and aligned into the S2 store-data register.
l1:l1.seq.store-hit.1.source: external/core-et/docs/FE-Intpipe-Description.pdf, pdf p.14 (§3.2.4); external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.24-25

l1:l1.seq.store-hit.2.statement: S2: data array read port. Reads the row being written (the store is a read-modify-write).
l1:l1.seq.store-hit.2.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.25 (text L955-957)

l1:l1.seq.store-hit.3.statement: S3: store merge / atomic unit. Merges the new bytes into the row read in S2.
l1:l1.seq.store-hit.3.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.26-27 (§3.1.4, Figure 7)

l1:l1.seq.store-hit.4.statement: S4: write-port arbiter; LRAM write port. Stores have the highest write priority. The per-block, per-half write enables and the 7-bit row address go to the macro; the write data was captured half a cycle earlier by the low-phase write-data latch; the decoded row's clock gate fires and that row's 64 latches turn transparent and take the new value.
l1:l1.seq.store-hit.4.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.27 (§3.1.5); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:3979-3980; the mechanism: external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/rf_latch_1r_1w_reg.v:88-136, tied to the LRAM only by external/core-et-main/docs/latch_translation.md:55-56, 93-96 (re-implementation)
l1:l1.seq.store-hit.4.kind_note: the write mechanism is the ET latch-RF pattern, assumed for the LRAM by the re-implementation's mapping; the silicon macro is asked

l1:l1.seq.store-hit.5.statement: S4 (first store to a clean line): miss handler, metadata array. A store to an exclusive (clean) line has the miss handler rewrite its metadata to modified (one 35-bit latch-RF write).
l1:l1.seq.store-hit.5.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.35 (text L1493-1495)

l1:l1.seq.store-hit.6.statement: S5: store bypass. Keeps the store data one more cycle so a younger load of the same bytes in S3 gets it.

l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.1.statement: S1: tag comparators; LRU. No way matches. The LRU matrix picks the victim way (locked ways excluded).

l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.2.statement: S2: miss handler (1 of 2); replay queue (8 entries). A free miss handler takes the miss (a second miss to the same line joins it); the load parks in the replay queue and the core carries on; the destination register is scoreboarded.
l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.2.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.34-35 (§3.6), pdf p.38-39 (§3.7-3.8); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_replay_queue.v:218-241

l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.3.statement: if the victim is dirty: miss handler Acquire_Wb; write-back unit. The write-back unit reads the victim's two rows (256 bits a cycle) and sends a 512-bit write on the evict interface to the L2.
l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.3.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.33 (text L1404-1407), pdf p.36 (Table 11)

l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.4.statement: Fill_Req: miss interface to the neighbourhood. Sends the line read to the L2 bank chosen by PA[7:6] (the L2 page takes over from here).
l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.4.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.36 (Table 11); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:479

l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.5.statement: Fill_Resp: neighbourhood fill FIFO; LRAM write port. The 512-bit response reaches the minion (at least 6 cycles through the neighbourhood's response path) and is written into the victim way's two rows through the write port, when no store holds it.
l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.5.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.27 (text L1128-1129), pdf p.33 (text L1437-1439); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.21 (text L826-834)
l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.5.note: Two writes follow from the 256-bit row width; the documents do not state the count.

l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.6.statement: Meta_Write_Req, Meta_Hazard: metadata latch RF; valid flip-flop. Writes the new tag and state (exclusive for a load) and sets valid; waits one hazard cycle.
l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.6.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.35-36 (§3.6.2, Table 11)

l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.7.statement: replay: replay queue -> S0 -> ... -> S3. The waiting load re-enters (the replay queue outranks new core requests), now hits, and returns its data.
l1:l1.seq.miss-refill.7.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.38-39 (text L1676-1688)

l1:l1.seq.scratchpad-read.1.statement: S1: VPU scratchpad request. The VPU sends way + address; any other S1 operation is cancelled into the replay queue; no TLB or tag check.

l1:l1.seq.scratchpad-read.2.statement: S2: data array, all 4 blocks. Reads one 256-bit row (8 lanes x 32 bits) from sets 0-11.

l1:l1.seq.scratchpad-read.3.statement: S3: s3_vpu_scp_data. Delivers the 256 bits to the VPU two cycles after the request.
l1:l1.seq.scratchpad-read.3.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.13 (text L447-448)

l1:l1.seq.tensorload.1.statement: CSR write: TensorLoad unit TL0. A tensor_load CSR write starts the FSM: per line, the address goes through S0/S1 for TLB and PMA checks.
l1:l1.seq.tensorload.1.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.15 (§2.3.4), pdf p.46 (§3.9.5)

l1:l1.seq.tensorload.2.statement: L2I FSMs: miss interface. Up to 4 line requests in flight to the L2.

l1:l1.seq.tensorload.3.statement: fill: LRAM write port. Each 512-bit response is written into the scratchpad line (the TensorLoad client of the write port).
l1:l1.seq.tensorload.3.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.33 (text L1440-1442), pdf p.40 (§3.9.1)

l1:l1.seq.refresh.1.statement: never: latch arrays. Nothing: latches hold their value while the minion rail is up, so the L1 has no refresh (the DRAM level does).

l2:l2.sc.what.statement: Each minion shire has one 4 MB shire cache whose storage is split by ESRs into three partitions: L2 (private to the shire), a slice of the chip-wide L3, and scratchpad. The L2 part serves the shire's 4 neighbourhoods (32 minions) and its RBOX.
l2:l2.sc.what.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.6 §1 and p.8 §1.1; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.13 §2.1.3.1

l2:l2.sc.chip-total.statement: The datasheet counts 140 MB of on-die SRAM, in 1 MB blocks each configurable as local L2, part of the chip-wide L3 or globally addressable scratchpad.
l2:l2.sc.chip-total.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 §1
l2:l2.sc.chip-total.note: 35 x 4 MB counts the I/O shire's cache; the Shire Cache Specification (pdf p.22) gives the I/O shire only 1 MB, a conflict the hub already lists under ask-design-docs.

l2:l2.partition.default.statement: Firmware default partition (Mode 0): 2.5 MB scratchpad, 0.5 MB L2, 1 MB L3 per shire (80 / 16 / 32 MB for the chip). The service processor reads the sizes from the card's flash configuration and writes them to every bank; the chip comes out of reset in M0.
l2:l2.partition.default.source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/minion_configuration.c:613-624; .../driver/bl2_cache_control.c:650-751; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.21-22 Table 6 and 'The chip will come out of reset in mode M0'; docs/reports/data/2026-09-22-cards/driver_config.json (l2_kb 16384, l3_kb 32768, scp_kb 81920 on every card)
l2:l2.partition.default.note: Every lab card's driver reports M0's sizes (docs/reports/data/2026-09-22-cards/driver_config.json). Latency plateaus up to 64 KB do not test the 512 KB edge.

l2:l2.partition.rows.statement: In Mode 0 the L2 occupies sets 0x280-0x2FF (128 of the 1,024 physical sets) of every sub-bank, set mask 0x7F: 4 banks x 4 sub-banks x 128 sets x 4 ways x 64 B = 512 KB. The scratchpad sits in sets 0x000-0x27F and the L3 in 0x300-0x3FF of the same RAMs.
l2:l2.partition.rows.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.22 Table 7 (Mode 0 rows); pdf p.25 §1.4.1.4 (physical set = region set + set_base)
l2:l2.partition.rows.note: So an L2 access lights only rows 640-767 of each tag/tag-state RAM and the matching {way,set} rows of the data RAMs; the other rows belong to scratchpad and L3.

l2:l2.private.statement: The L2 is private to its shire and not coherent: it does not track ownership or sharing across the 32 minions it serves; software handles coherence.
l2:l2.private.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.6 §1; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.13 §2.1.3.1

l2:l2.assoc.statement: The L2 is 4-way set associative with 64-byte lines, write-back and write-allocate, and uses LRU replacement stored as a 5-bit code per set (4! = 24 orders).

l2:l2.banks.statement: The shire cache is four identical banks; each bank is an independent L2 cache with its own request queue, pipeline and next-level ports. A bank takes at most one request per cycle and returns at most one 512-bit line per cycle.

l2:l2.bank-select.statement: L2 and scratchpad requests go to the bank chosen by PA[7:6], so consecutive 64 B lines rotate through banks 0-3.

l2:l2.decode.statement: L2 address fields: offset PA[5:0], bank PA[7:6], sub-bank PA[9:8], set from PA[10] (PA[19:10] for a full 4 MB L2; PA[16:10] with Mode 0's 7-bit set mask), tag above. The tag RAM stores 23 tag bits, which 'allows for down to 512k L2 allocation'.

l2:l2.subbanks.statement: Each bank is four sub-banks. Each sub-bank has its own tag RAM, tag-state RAM, data RAM and ECC logic; the read buffer, atomic unit and coalescing buffer are shared by the bank's four sub-banks.
l2:l2.subbanks.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.35 §2.5; pdf p.9 ('4 sub-banks/bank' is the POR for the first SoC)

l2:l2.sets.statement: A sub-bank holds 4,096 lines = 1,024 sets x 4 ways (4 MB / 64 B / 4 banks / 4 sub-banks).

l2:l2.tag-ram.statement: Tag RAM: one row per set holding all four ways' tags, each 23 bits + 6 ECC bits, so the row is 116 bits and the four tags are read and compared in parallel.
l2:l2.tag-ram.note: The overview (pdf p.9) says '7 bits of ECC stored with each 33-bit tag'; §2.14.2, the defines and the 1024x116 macro all say 23 + 6.

l2:l2.tag-state-ram.statement: Tag-state RAM: one 40-bit row per set = 4 x {valid, locked, zero, qwen[3:0]} + 5-bit LRU code + 7-bit ECC. It is read and written on every L2 request, and it is two-ported, so the read and the LRU/dirty update happen in the same pass.
l2:l2.tag-state-ram.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.47 §2.14.3 Table 12 and pdf p.45; external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:231-237

l2:l2.data-ram.statement: Data RAM: each sub-bank is four 144-bit-wide panels, each holding one 128-bit quadword + 16 ECC bits (8 per 64 bits). A 64 B line is one row across the four panels (576 bits); a sub-bank's data RAM is 4,096 rows addressed by {way, set}.

l2:l2.serial-lookup.statement: The lookup is serial (tag first, then data): the data-RAM address includes the way, and the data stages (dap..dc) start after the tag compare (tc), so a hit reads only the hit way's row, not all four ways.
l2:l2.serial-lookup.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:253 (SC_DATA_RAM_ADDR_SIZE = way + set); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.44 read-hit stage figure

l2:l2.panel-select.statement: Only the panels holding the addressed quadwords are enabled (a 3-quadword partial write activates 3 panels), and the RAM inputs, address bits included, are held unchanged in cycles with no access, to save power.

l2:l2.macro.data.statement: The data panel is the compiled macro 'saduls0g4l1p4096x144m4b4w0c0p0d0s1rm0sdrw11', RAM type 1PUHD: 4,096 words x 144 bits.
l2:l2.macro.data.note: The spec gives the type code, not its meaning. Reading 1PUHD as single-port ultra-high-density follows common memory-compiler naming (GENERIC); no source states it.

l2:l2.macro.tag.statement: The tag RAM is 'saduls0g4l1p1024x116m4b1w0c0p0d0s1rm0sdrw11', type 1PUHD: 1,024 words x 116 bits.

l2:l2.macro.state.statement: The tag-state RAM is 'saculs0g4l2p1024x40m4b1w0c0p0d0s1rm0rw11', RAM type 2PUHDRF: 1,024 words x 40 bits. The spec says the state RAM is two-ported (a read and a write per request).
l2:l2.macro.state.note: Reading 'RF' in 2PUHDRF as register file follows common memory-compiler naming (GENERIC); no source states it.

l2:l2.macro.vendor.statement: The tag-state, tag and data panels are 'IP acquired from a third party vendor'. They are tested with a shared-bus BIST 'such as the Synopsys SMS (STAR Memory System)'. The BIST's logical RAMs per bank are mbs (tag state), mbt (tag), mbd (data), mbq (dataq) and mbi (instruction cache, bank 0 only).
l2:l2.macro.vendor.note: The vendor and bitcell are not named. The Synopsys BIST and the name pattern point to a Synopsys-compiled memory, but that is an inference.

l2:l2.macro.count.statement: Per shire there are 64 data macros (4 banks x 4 sub-banks x 4 panels), 16 tag macros and 16 tag-state macros.
l2:l2.macro.count.source: derived from external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.48 §2.14.5, p.47 §2.14.2-3 and p.51

l2:l2.bits.statement: Bits stored per shire, ECC included: data 64 x 4,096 x 144 = 37,748,736; tag 16 x 1,024 x 116 = 1,900,544; tag state 16 x 1,024 x 40 = 655,360; 40,304,640 in all (about 40.3 Mbit, of which 33.6 Mbit is the 4 MB of data).
l2:l2.bits.source: derived from the macro sizes, external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.51

l2:l2.transistors.statement: If the single-port data and tag macros use a 6-transistor cell and the two-port tag-state file an 8-transistor cell (the usual choice for such macros), one shire's cache arrays hold about 243 million cell transistors (39.6 Mbit x 6 + 0.66 Mbit x 8), before any periphery.
l2:l2.transistors.note: GENERIC assumption: the ET bitcell is not documented (see l2.storage-question).

l2:l2.macro.name-decode.statement: Reading 'm4' and 'b4' in the data macro's name as a memory compiler's column-mux 4 and internal-bank 4 fields would make each 4096x144 panel about 1,024 wordlines by 576 bitline pairs, split into 4 banks, with each output bit chosen from 4 columns. No source defines the fields.
l2:l2.macro.name-decode.note: This is naming-convention inference. The macro datasheet settles it.

l2:l2.trim.statement: Each logical RAM group has ESR trim bits: RM (read margin), RME (RM enable), RA (read assist), WA (write assist) and WPULSE (write-pulse width). They default to 'RM0 mode to allow nominal 650mV operation'. For the 1PUHD tag and data macros the table gives RM0 = VMIN 585 mV, Vnom 650: RM 0, WA 7, RA 1, WPULSE 0. For the 2PUHDRF tag-state RAM it gives RM0 = VMIN 540 mV: WA 6, RA 2. The tables run up to RM5 at 855 mV VMIN.
l2:l2.trim.unit: mV nominal at the default trim

l2:l2.trim.reset.statement: The simulator's reset values for shire_cache_ram_cfg1/2 (0xE800340, 0x03A0), decoded with the HAL's field layout, are exactly the tables' RM0 rows: tag and data RAMs RM=0, RA=1, WA=7, WPULSE=0 with RME=0; tag-state RA=2, WA=6. No firmware in et-platform at 836a4ab writes these registers.
l2:l2.trim.reset.source: external/et-platform/sw-sysemu/esrs_et.cpp:46-47; external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/hwinc/etsoc_shire_other_esr.h:3070-3376 (field bit positions); grep of et-platform for RAM_CFG writes (none)
l2:l2.trim.reset.note: Whether the boot ROM or silicon reset programs something else is not known (ask). If they do not, the arrays run with the 650 mV assist settings at the rail's ~705 mV.

l2:l2.storage-question.statement: What the storage circuit is on silicon is not settled. The Shire Cache Specification calls the data array 'SRAM memory panels' and the datasheet calls it 140 MB of SRAM, but the lab lead said the chip is 'not using SRAM'. No source gives the bitcell (6T, 8T or other) or confirms that the v1.1 macros are the ones taped out.
l2:l2.storage-question.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.40 §2.8 and p.48 §2.14.5; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 §1
l2:l2.storage-question.note: For contrast, the L1 data cache is documented as not SRAM: 4 LRAM (latch-RAM) blocks of 128 rows x 64 bits (external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29). The remark may refer to the L1 and register files rather than the shire cache.

l2:l2.l1-context.statement: Context for the 'not SRAM' question: the minion's L1 data cache is built from 4 LRAM (latch-based RAM) blocks of 128 rows x 64 bits, not SRAM; the reimplementation names its model dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram.
l2:l2.l1-context.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29 and p.61 (glossary 'LRAM Latch Random Access Memory'); external/core-et/rtl/libs/macros/dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram.v:1-12

l2:l2.clock.statement: The shire cache runs on shire_clock from the shire's PLL. The neighbourhoods (minions) run on the same clock shifted by 180 degrees (a DLL), and the errata note that every area of a minion shire except the NoC uses the same clock. So one shire-cache cycle is one minion cycle.
l2:l2.clock.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.12 Table 2; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.39 Table 6; external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf, pdf p.42

l2:l2.freq.statement: The firmware reports the L2/SRAM frequency as equal to the minion frequency: 600 MHz at the governor's operating point used for every measurement here.

l2:l2.domain.statement: The Shire Channel (shire cache, UC block, ESRs, instruction-cache memories) is a separate high-voltage (HV) region on the shire clock. The minions and most of each neighbourhood are a low-voltage (LV) region on the neighbourhood clock. Each neighbourhood's north ports are the HV interface. The instruction-cache data memory sits in the Shire Channel 'because it has to be operated at high voltage'.
l2:l2.domain.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.5 Figure 1 (legend 'HV Region'), pdf p.10 §3.1; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.6-7 §2, pdf p.45 §7

l2:l2.rail.sram.statement: The card's VDD_SRAM regulator feeds the shire-cache SRAM arrays (L2/L3/scratchpad); it is one of the three rails whose power the PMIC meters. In every measurement here its set point was 705 mV (703-707 mV read on the die); 750 mV is the card's power-tree figure (20 A / 15 W) and the firmware's boot default.
l2:l2.rail.sram.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace-telemetry.jsonl and horace2-telemetry.jsonl (reg_mv.sram = 705 in all 586 + 1,247 samples, die_mv.sram 704); docs/research/power-telemetry.md:46 (power tree), :189-190 (boot defaults: 'SRAM 750'; thermal_pwr_mgmt.h; bl2_pmic_controller.h:165-244)

l2:l2.rail.hv-logic.statement: Whether VDD_SRAM also powers the rest of the HV region (request queues, crossbars, read buffers, ECC, the voltage-crossing FIFO cells, the instruction-cache memories) or only the RAM macros is not stated. The Power Spec that would say is not in the documents we have.
l2:l2.rail.hv-logic.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.18 §5 (refers to the Power Spec)

l2:l2.voltage.idle.statement: Measured on-die SRAM-rail voltage per shire at idle: 703-707 mV across the 34 minion shires (minion rail 513-522 mV, mesh 483-486 mV).

l2:l2.voltage.limits.statement: The firmware limits the SRAM rail to 660-850 mV, and DVFS moves the minion and L2/SRAM voltages together.

l2:l2.vc-fifo.statement: The neighbourhood's per-bank output FIFOs double as the clock- and voltage-crossing elements: semi-synchronous VC FIFOs from the cell library, with level shifters built in at the HV/LV boundary. Their storage cells always sit in the HV region 'as performance and access time improve with the voltage'. Responses cross back through a VC FIFO at the neighbourhood's input.
l2:l2.vc-fifo.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.18-19 §4.3.4, pdf p.20 §4.4.1, pdf p.45 §7.1 (Figure 16)

l2:l2.path.miss.statement: An L1 miss starts one of the minion's two miss handlers, which asks the L2 for the line. Loads leave on the miss interface (3 valid/ready pairs: regular, TensorLoad 0, TensorLoad 1). Stores, evicts, atomics and messages leave on the 256-bit evict interface.
l2:l2.path.miss.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.15 Table 2; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.34-36 §3.6; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:448

l2:l2.path.nbr-request.statement: Inside the neighbourhood a request passes the minion's Miss/Evict flip-flops, a 2:1 minion arbiter (evicts first), a flop, a two-stage 13:1 round-robin arbiter, a 1-cycle pre-processing stage and then one of five output FIFOs (four banks + UC, 3 entries each, with a 2-entry intermediate FIFO). Minimum latency for a minion's request is 6 cycles.

l2:l2.path.widths.statement: The neighbourhood's request datapath is 256 bits wide (a 512-bit write takes two cycles and is re-joined before the bank FIFO); its response datapath and the ET-Link into each bank are 512 bits; the minion's own fill interface is 256 bits, so a 64 B line reaches the L1 in two beats.
l2:l2.path.widths.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.14-15 §4.3, p.19 §4.3.5, p.20 §4.4, p.22-23 §4.4.3; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.10 §1.1

l2:l2.xbar.req.statement: req_xbar: a full crossbar from the 5 clients (4 neighbourhoods + RBOX) to the 4 banks + UC. Each bank has one catch FIFO per neighbourhood and a round-robin arbiter that skips entries whose bank is stalled. It lives in the shire-cache hierarchy 'so that it can be routed on top of all four banks'.

l2:l2.xbar.rsp.statement: rsp_xbar: the same module in reverse (4 banks + UC to 4 neighbourhoods + RBOX). Neighbourhoods never back-pressure, since space for the response is reserved. It arbitrates only when two banks answer the same neighbourhood in one cycle.

l2:l2.nbr.response.statement: Back in the neighbourhood a response goes through the VC FIFO (min 2 cycles), the Fill FIFO (a 4-entry buffer drained out of order by an LRU 4:1 arbiter, min 2 cycles) and the minion's Fill FF, which splits 512 bits into two 256-bit beats (min 2 cycles): 6 cycles minimum for a minion.

l2:l2.reqq.statement: Each bank has a 64-entry request queue (reqq), the equivalent of MSHRs. An entry lives from allocation through miss, mesh read, fill and any victim write-back. Two entries can be allocated per cycle (one neighbourhood, one L3-slave request), and 21 of the 64 are reserved for L3-slave requests by default.

l2:l2.reqq.arb.statement: Choosing what enters the pipeline takes three steps: round-robin per sub-bank (neighbourhood and L3 separately), then L3 requests before neighbourhood requests, then masking out busy sub-banks and a round-robin across sub-banks. Errata RTLMIN-6207 and 6214 record that a neighbourhood request can starve behind L3-slave traffic.
l2:l2.reqq.arb.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.36 §2.6 Figure 8; external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf, pdf p.80-81 §4.1-4.2
l2:l2.reqq.arb.page: One hot line stops a shire

l2:l2.reqq.order.statement: Requests to the same address keep their order through per-address linked lists in the reqq. A victim is inserted at the front, so a later read miss cannot fetch the line before its write-back is acknowledged.

l2:l2.dataq.statement: The dataq holds one 64 B line per reqq entry in a two-ported register file (one write and one read port, each shared by 5 sources). BIST sees it as logical RAM mbq (64 x 4 x 144 bits, 1-cycle access) plus mbb (64 x 72 bits). Read hits normally bypass it straight to the response mux.
l2:l2.dataq.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.35, pdf p.38-40 §2.7, pdf p.49; external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:350-380

l2:l2.subbank-busy.statement: With 2-cycle RAMs a sub-bank accepts a new request only every other cycle (3-cycle RAMs: every third). Operations that need two RAM passes (a fill that may evict, an atomic) reserve bubble slots, because the pipeline never stalls once a request is scheduled.
l2:l2.subbank-busy.unit: cycles between requests to one sub-bank

l2:l2.ramdelay.statement: RAM access time is 2, 3 or 4 cycles, one setting (esr_sc_ram_delay) for all three RAM types, set at boot. The design intends 2, which is the default.
l2:l2.ramdelay.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.9, pdf p.48 §2.14.6.1, pdf p.101; external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:260
l2:l2.ramdelay.note: The value programmed on the cards has not been read.

l2:l2.stages.statement: Read-hit pipeline stages (2-cycle RAMs): ag (reqq allocate), ad (dependencies), rqa (reqq arbitration), tap, ta, ta0, ta1 (tag and tag-state RAM access), te (tag ECC), tc (tag compare: hit, victim), dap, da, da0, da1 (data RAM access), de (data ECC), dc (data complete: OR'd across the sub-banks, then to the response mux, or the dataq if the mux is busy).

l2:l2.stages.budget.statement: If each named stage is one cycle, the 15 stages from reqq allocation to data complete account for 15 of the spec's 21-cycle L2 hit, leaving about 6 cycles for the request crossbar, response mux and response crossbar. The spec cites an 'L2 and L3 Pipeline stages Spreadsheet' that has the real budget, which we do not have.
l2:l2.stages.budget.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.11 Table 1, pdf p.44-46, pdf p.131 ref. 3
l2:l2.stages.budget.note: One cycle per stage is an assumption.

l2:l2.throughput.statement: Consecutive operations to different sub-banks can issue every cycle. Operations that can create a victim (fills, writes, write-arounds, locks) run at one per 4, 6 or 8 cycles per sub-bank (RAM delay 2, 3, 4), because read and write slots are both reserved. The tag is written 4 cycles after the victim is chosen (2-cycle RAMs).

l2:l2.rbuf.statement: Read buffer (RBUF): an 8-entry fully associative mini-cache of clean lines per bank (2 KB per shire). Lines are installed on L2 and scratchpad read hits. Requests are checked against it when they are allocated a reqq entry, and hits are served from it without touching the RAM panels, 'as these memory panels are slow and power hungry'. Anything that will change the data RAM clears the entry, and a 4-entry FIFO holds hit responses.

l2:l2.rbuf.enabled.statement: The RBUF is on by default (esr_sc_l2_rbuf_enable = esr_sc_scp_rbuf_enable = 1 in the RTL's ESR init), and the cards show it: a 36-cycle plateau for working sets of 768 B to 2 KB, then 47 cycles from 4 KB, on all three cards.

l2:l2.rbuf.storage.statement: What the RBUF is built from on silicon is not documented. The Ainekko reimplementation keeps it as 8 x 512-bit registers (flip-flops) holding ECC-corrected data, with an LRU replacement arbiter and a 7-stage pending-install pipeline.

l2:l2.cbuf.statement: Each bank has a 32-entry coalescing buffer that merges write-arounds (TensorStores to L3 or a remote scratchpad) in the L2. It flushes a line once all four 128-bit quadwords are written, or on an explicit flush.

l2:l2.atomic.statement: Each bank has an atomic unit (32-, 64- and 256-bit operands: swap, add, and, or, xor, min/max signed and unsigned, float min/max). An atomic keeps its sub-bank busy from the read through the operation to the write.

l2:l2.zero-state.statement: Each way's tag state has a 'zero' bit: the data RAM is not read and zeros are returned. REQ_Lock sets it (a missing line is installed without a fill), and esr_sc_zero_state_enable (default 1) 'prevents reading/writing from the data RAMs if the content of the data is all zeros'. A fill or a full-line write of an all-zero line sets it (the bank computes the NOR of the 512 bits as the line arrives).
l2:l2.zero-state.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.47 Table 12, pdf p.78 §3.9, pdf p.101; external/core-et-main/hw/ip/shirecache/rtl/shirecache_bank_mesh.sv:346 (zero_data = ~|data), shirecache_pipe_sub_bank.sv:983-1001, 1051-1063 (re-implementation RTL)
l2:l2.zero-state.note: Whether a partial write that leaves a line all zero sets the bit is not stated (asked). It matters for reading the zeros-vs-random energy gap.

l2:l2.ecc.statement: All shire-cache RAMs have SECDED ECC (single-error correct, double-error detect): 6 bits per tag, 7 per tag-state row and 8 per 64 data bits, checked in stages te and de. On this chip ECC covers only the L2/L3/scratchpad SRAM and the instruction cache. Background ECC scrubbing is a reserved bit, 'implemented in Gepardo', a later chip.
l2:l2.ecc.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.9, pdf p.48-49 §2.14.6.2, pdf p.99; docs/findings/15-earlier-findings.md:65-66

l2:l2.sleep.statement: The RAMs can be put into deep sleep (low-leakage retention) or shut down only for shires that are not operational (esr_sc_ram_deep_sleep / esr_sc_ram_shut_down). The cards show no array wake-up: an L2 hit reads 49.5 cycles after any idle from 1.7 us to 27 ms.

l2:l2.clock-gating.statement: Module-level clock gaters (esr_sc_clk_gate_disable) stop the bank's clock when it has no outstanding requests (errata RTLMIN-6235, which is why the bank's cycle counter under-counts). The reimplementation gates each RAM's clock on only for the ram_delay cycles of an access.
l2:l2.clock-gating.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.97 §4.1; external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf, pdf p.82 §4.3; external/core-et-main/hw/ip/shirecache/rtl/shirecache_pipe_data_ram_wrap.sv:1-7, 46-66
l2:l2.clock-gating.note: The per-access RAM clock enable is from the Ainekko reimplementation, not the ET-SoC-1 RTL.

l2:l2.power-goal.statement: The spec's power target is 'TBD. Goal is 100 MW for the entire Shire Cache running benchmark'. The unit is presumably mW.

l2:l2.all-inv.statement: At power-up the index CacheOp state machine runs Idx_All_Inv, which writes zeros to every way of the tag-state RAM, one index per cycle, starting about 256 clocks after reset (skipped if BIST is running).

l2:l2.spec-version.statement: The Shire Cache Specification in hand is v1.1 from core-et's Erbium branch. It also documents later variants ('Atomic (with NEMI)', ECC scrub 'implemented in Gepardo'), while it calls '4M/Shire, 4 banks/Shire, 4 sub-banks/bank' the POR for the first SoC. Latencies measured on the cards match its Table 1 up to a constant (l2.lat.overhead).
l2:l2.spec-version.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.1, p.4 §3.8, p.9, p.99; docs/reports/2026-09-18-et-soc1-memory-hierarchy.html:915 (sources note)
l2:l2.spec-version.note: Facts marked et-spec from this document are for the design; where silicon could differ (macros, trims, partition) the diagram should say so.

l2:l2.hpf.statement: The original RTL had an L2 hardware-prefetcher interface (shire_cache_bank_l2hpf). The reimplementation stubs it out by default (L2HpfImplemented = 0; 'assumes shire cache bank read buffer not enabled'). No source says whether ET-SoC-1 silicon has an L2 prefetcher; the L1 has none.

l2:l2.floorplan.statement: Where the four banks, their sixteen sub-banks and 96 macros sit inside the shire tile, and how long the crossbar wires to each neighbourhood are, is in no source; Figure 1 of the Minion Shire Description is a logical diagram.
l2:l2.floorplan.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.5 Figure 1

l2:l2.perfmon.statement: Each bank has a performance monitor: a cycle counter and two 40-bit event counters, which can count RBUF hits, tag hits and misses, victims and opcodes. They are M-mode registers. A U-mode kernel can only read them (syscall 9) with the firmware's default qualifier, which counts all read-type requests and does not separate hits from misses.

l2:l2.lat.spec.statement: Idle-cache latencies in shire clocks, from the neighbourhood's ET-Link request to its response, crossbars included: L2 hit 21, read-buffer hit 10, L2 miss 34 + NoC and L3/memory latency.

l2:l2.lat.measured.statement: Load-to-use latency by pointer chase at 600 MHz: read-buffer hit 36.00 cycles (60 ns) and L2 or own-scratchpad hit 47.00 cycles (78 ns) on hart 0; hart 1 pays 3 more (39.0 and 50.0). Every pass on every card fell within 35.998-36.006 and 46.998-47.024.

l2:l2.lat.overhead.statement: Measured minus spec is 26 cycles for both (47 - 21 = 36 - 10), so the path outside the shire cache is a constant and the 11-cycle read-buffer saving is all inside the bank. That is consistent with one shire clock being one minion cycle (l2.clock). Of the 26, the neighbourhood's request and response datapaths take at least 6 + 6, leaving about 14 for the minion's L1 miss detection, miss handler and fill-to-use.
l2:l2.lat.overhead.source: derived from external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.11 Table 1, docs/findings/05-claims.md:421 and external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.20-21

l2:l2.lat.ladder.statement: Timing one load after an evict_va to L2 gives two populations: about 37 cycles when the line is still in the bank's read buffer and 48 from the array. The 19 September histogram has 37: 2,187, 38: 780, 48: 1,117, 49: 407 loads over 1,500 lines x 3. The version-3 ladder median is 49 cycles on every card.
l2:l2.lat.ladder.note: memprobe's timer correction (workloads/memprobe/README.md:36-39: subtract 5 so a timed L1 hit reads 5) is not the pointer chase's method; its 37/48 correspond to the chase's 36/47.

l2:l2.lat.miss.statement: A local L3 hit costs 110 cycles, of which about 48 are the L1 and L2 lookups and the L2 miss (if a miss costs what a hit does) and about 62 are the home slice; each mesh hop adds 12 cycles.

l2:l2.bw.measured.statement: With 1 KB tensor loads on every minion the L2 delivers 2.45 TB/s chip-wide: 4.0 B per minion-cycle = 128 B per shire-cycle, half the four banks' 256 B per shire-cycle. The own scratchpad gives the same (2.46 TB/s).

l2:l2.bw.per-bank.statement: 128 B per shire-cycle is one 64 B line every 2 cycles per bank (0.5 lines per bank-cycle). The rate is exact (3.999-4.000 B per minion-cycle, the same for L2 and scratchpad), which points to a structural 2-cycle limit rather than a latency or concurrency limit. The spec lets a bank return one line per cycle when successive requests go to different sub-banks, and 1 KB tensor loads do rotate sub-banks (PA[9:8]).
l2:l2.bw.per-bank.source: derived from l2.bw.measured and external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.6, p.44
l2:l2.bw.per-bank.note: Which block sets the 2-cycle limit is unknown (ask).

l2:l2.bw.gather.statement: Random-word gathers from the L2 (one line per element) reach 27.4 G lines/s chip-wide, 1.15x the bound set by two miss handlers per minion. A second hart adds nothing.

l2:l2.e.level.statement: Reading the L2 with 1 KB tensor loads on every minion at 600 MHz costs 3.11 pJ/B [1.42-4.99] above idle (per card: aifoundry2 2.64, aifoundry3 2.83, aifoundry1-c1 3.86). That is about 199 pJ per 64 B line for the whole path.
l2:l2.e.level.note: The buffer's contents were not set; the scratchpad rows below control the data.

l2:l2.e.scp-contents.statement: The same arrays read as the shire's own scratchpad (no tag compare) cost 2.25 pJ/B [2.06-2.61] filled with zeros and 4.40 [3.94-5.08] filled with random data: about 144 vs 282 pJ per 64 B line, 2x for the data.

l2:l2.e.tload-tstore.statement: Tensor load from the own scratchpad: 2.12 (zeros) / 4.43 (random) pJ/B. Tensor store into it: 4.65 / 8.58 pJ/B. A scratchpad write costs about twice a read.

l2:l2.e.l2-minus-scp.statement: At a steady 600 MHz the L2 costs about what the scratchpad costs per byte: pass by pass, the L2-minus-scratchpad difference includes zero on each card. The tag lookup does not show up in board power.

l2:l2.e.rails.statement: No L2 hit has been split between the rails on three cards. Read as the shire's own scratchpad (1 KB tensor loads, no tag check, random data), the same arrays put 69, 68 and 49% of the power above idle on the SRAM rail, 24, 23 and 21% on the minion rail, 1% or less on the mesh and 7, 9 and 29% on no metered rail (aifoundry2, aifoundry3 and aifoundry1 card 1; the energy manual's catalogue, 26 September).
l2:l2.e.rails.unit: % on the SRAM rail (own-scratchpad read, aifoundry2)
l2:l2.e.rails.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.cards.<card>.summary['tload/scp/random'] (rails_over_w, over_idle_w), as Anatomy of a memory access §6 splits it (workloads/memprobe/build_report.py)
l2:l2.e.rails.note: Until 28 September this row gave the first measurement, on 19 September on aifoundry2 alone (an L2 hit by 8-byte loads; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json power.l2); Anatomy of a memory access keeps those runs as one note, and its §6 shows this split. The unmetered share is highest on the card whose unmetered power rises most with its SRAM rail's (the energy manual's fit of the unmetered power, §4.5: unmetered.<card>.coef.sram).

l2:l2.e.bit.statement: Streaming TensorLoads from the L2 at 2.4 TB/s adds 6.2 W: 2.6 pJ/B = 0.3 pJ per bit, a switched capacitance of 0.038 nF per minion.

l2:l2.e.l1fill.statement: Filling one 64 B line from the scratchpad into the L1: 101 pJ on zeros and 205 pJ on random data (both cards pooled).

l2:l2.e.scalar.statement: One random flw from the L2 (a line per load) costs 336 pJ [315-369] at 27.5 G/s. One fsw costs 774 pJ: the store allocates the line and writes it back.

l2:l2.e.gather-line.statement: A gather from the L2 costs 104 pJ per instruction plus 338 pJ per line it fetches (least-squares fit over seven patterns).

l2:l2.e.shire.statement: At full L2 bandwidth (2.45 TB/s at 3.11 pJ/B), the whole path draws about 7.6 W above idle, about 240 mW per shire. If an L2 read puts as large a share on the SRAM rail as a read of the same arrays as the own scratchpad does (49-69%, by card; l2.e.rails), roughly 115-165 mW of that is on the SRAM rail, the same order as the spec's 100 mW goal.
l2:l2.e.shire.source: derived from l2.bw.measured, l2.e.level, l2.e.rails, l2.power-goal

l2:l2.leak.statement: SRAM-rail power at idle: 2.00 W for the chip (about 16 mW per MB if split evenly over the 128 MB of L2, L3 and scratchpad, the energy manual's denominator); 1.70 W at 67 C and 2.73 W at 82 C on aifoundry2; 0.051-0.066 W per degree C on the other cards.
l2:l2.leak.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md:184, 473; docs/findings/16-dvfs-and-leakage.md:141; docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md:110 ('Measured: 1.70 W at 67 °C') and its table (67 °C 1.698 W, 82 °C 2.726 W)
l2:l2.leak.note: The per-MB split assumes the rail feeds the 128 MB evenly; what else is on the rail is unknown (asked).

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.01.statement: minion L1 / miss handler (LV region, minion rail): The load misses the L1; one of the two miss handlers allocates and puts a line-fill request (REQ_Read, line address) on the miss interface into the neighbourhood's Miss FF.
l2:l2.seq.load-hit.01.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.15-16 §4.3.1; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.34-36 §3.6

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.02.statement: neighbourhood request datapath -> bank FIFO (LV -> HV crossing): 2:1 minion arbiter, 13:1 round-robin arbiter, pre-processing, then the output FIFO of the bank picked by PA[7:6]. That FIFO is a semi-synchronous VC FIFO whose cells sit in the HV region, with level shifters at the boundary.

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.03.statement: request crossbar (req_xbar): The request enters its bank's catch FIFO for that neighbourhood, and the bank's round-robin arbiter admits it (one request per bank per cycle). The crossbar is routed on top of the four banks.

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.04.statement: reqq allocate (stages ag, ad): A reqq entry is allocated. The address is compared with every in-flight entry (ordering) and with the 8 RBUF tags. Here the RBUF misses, so the request is eligible for the pipeline.
l2:l2.seq.load-hit.04.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.37 §2.6.1, pdf p.40 §2.8, pdf p.45 §2.14.1.1-2

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.05.statement: reqq arbitration (stage rqa): Round-robin per sub-bank, L3 requests first, busy sub-banks masked; the winner's information is muxed out of the reqq.

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.06.statement: tag RAM + tag-state RAM of one sub-bank (stages tap, ta, ta0, ta1): The sub-bank chosen by PA[9:8] reads the set's row (a Mode 0 L2 set lives in rows 0x280-0x2FF): the 116-bit tag row (all four tags + ECC) from the 1024x116 single-port macro and the 40-bit state row from the 1024x40 two-port file. The other sub-banks' RAM inputs stay frozen.
l2:l2.seq.load-hit.06.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.44-46, pdf p.47 §2.14.2-3, pdf p.51

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.07.statement: tag ECC (stage te): SECDED check and repair of each way's 23+6-bit tag.

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.08.statement: tag compare (stage tc) + tag-state write: Four 23-bit comparators find the hit way. The new LRU code (5 bits) and flags are written back through the tag-state file's write port in the same pass, and hit/victim status goes to the reqq.
l2:l2.seq.load-hit.08.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.45 (state RAM two-ported), pdf p.46 §2.14.1.9, pdf p.47-48 §2.14.4

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.09.statement: data RAM, 4 panels of one sub-bank (stages dap, da, da0, da1): Row {hit way, set} is read from the four 4096x144 panels: 4 x 144 = 576 bits (512 data + 64 ECC). Only this sub-bank's data macros are clocked; a partial access would enable fewer panels.
l2:l2.seq.load-hit.09.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.44-46, pdf p.48 §2.14.5, pdf p.51; external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:253

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.10.statement: data ECC (stage de): Eight SECDED checks, one per 64-bit dword (8 check bits each), correcting single-bit errors.

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.11.statement: data complete (stage dc) + RBUF install: The line is OR'd with the other (idle) sub-banks' outputs and sent to the response mux (or parked in the dataq if the mux is busy). It is installed in the bank's read buffer.

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.12.statement: response mux (rspmux) + response crossbar: Per-neighbourhood queue and arbiter, then rsp_xbar back to the requesting neighbourhood.

l2:l2.seq.load-hit.13.statement: neighbourhood response path (HV -> LV) -> L1 fill -> load completes: VC FIFO (level shifters back down to the minion rail), Fill FIFO, the minion's Fill FF splits the line into two 256-bit beats, the DCache writes the line and the load returns its word.
l2:l2.seq.load-hit.13.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf pdf p.21-23; docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md:27; docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md:44 (the L1 fill, three cards)

l2:l2.seq.load-rbuf-hit.01.statement: minion -> neighbourhood -> req_xbar: As load-hit steps 1-3.

l2:l2.seq.load-rbuf-hit.02.statement: reqq allocate: RBUF tag match: The address matches one of the bank's 8 RBUF entries at allocation, so the request goes to the RBUF instead of the pipeline. No tag, tag-state or data macro is accessed.

l2:l2.seq.load-rbuf-hit.03.statement: RBUF read -> RBUF FIFO -> rspmux: The entry's 512 bits are read out (an 8:1 mux over registers in the reimplementation) into the 4-entry RBUF FIFO, then the response mux.

l2:l2.seq.load-rbuf-hit.04.statement: rsp_xbar -> neighbourhood -> L1: As load-hit steps 12-13.

l2:l2.seq.store-writeback.01.statement: minion L1 evict (dirty line): The L1 is write-back: a store stays in the L1 until its line is evicted. The eviction is a full-line REQ_Write sent as two 256-bit transfers on the evict interface, re-joined in the Evict FF (+1 cycle, 3 in all).
l2:l2.seq.store-writeback.01.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.33; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.16-17 §4.3.1

l2:l2.seq.store-writeback.02.statement: neighbourhood -> req_xbar (512-bit request takes 2 cycles): The same path as a load, but with data: 512-bit requests are served every other cycle.

l2:l2.seq.store-writeback.03.statement: reqq + dataq write: A reqq entry is allocated and the 64 B of data are written into its dataq entry (one of the 5 dataq write sources).

l2:l2.seq.store-writeback.04.statement: pipeline L2_Write: tag + tag-state read, compare: As load-hit steps 6-8. The dirty bits (qwen = 0xF) and LRU are updated in the state write.

l2:l2.seq.store-writeback.05.statement: data RAM write (hit way): The data comes back out of the dataq and is written to row {way, set} of the four panels (only panels with written quadwords are enabled). If the tag missed, the LRU way is the victim: a clean victim is dropped silently, and a dirty one is read in a reserved slot, then overwritten and sent to L3 on to_l3. A full-line write needs no fill.
l2:l2.seq.store-writeback.05.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.44-45, pdf p.48, pdf p.58-59 §3.4.1 Figure 18

l2:l2.seq.store-writeback.06.statement: REP_Ack back to the minion: Sent as soon as the cache write completes; the reqq entry frees when any victim's mesh write is acknowledged.

l2:l2.seq.miss-refill.01.statement: tag compare misses (stage tc): As load-hit steps 1-8. No way matches, so tc reports a miss to the reqq and the data stages are skipped for this pass.

l2:l2.seq.miss-refill.02.statement: bank mesh (to_l3 master) -> NoC: The reqq issues Mesh_Read on the bank's 512-bit to_l3 port. It is arbitrated with the other banks onto 4 mesh lanes and crosses to the NoC clock and voltage through a VCFIFO with 2-stage synchronizers. The read goes to the line's home L3 slice (see the L3 diagram).
l2:l2.seq.miss-refill.02.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.8, pdf p.11 (VCFIFO), pdf p.32-33 §2.3, pdf p.43 §2.11

l2:l2.seq.miss-refill.03.statement: fill data returns: The mesh response goes straight to the neighbourhood (lowest latency) and is also written into the reqq entry's dataq line.

l2:l2.seq.miss-refill.04.statement: L2_Fill through the pipeline: The tag-state read picks the LRU way (never a locked way). If that way is dirty (qwen != 0), its data row is read first in a reserved slot, becoming the victim. Then the new tag, state and 576-bit data row are written. The pipeline reserves both slots, so a fill runs at one per 4 cycles per sub-bank.
l2:l2.seq.miss-refill.04.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.44-45, pdf p.47-48, pdf p.54-55

l2:l2.seq.miss-refill.05.statement: victim write-back: A dirty victim goes to to_l3 as a write (straight from the pipeline if the mesh is free, else via the dataq). Later reads of that address queue behind it; the entry frees when the write is acknowledged.
l2:l2.seq.miss-refill.05.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.37 (victims head the linked list), pdf p.54-55

l2:l2.seq.no-refresh.01.statement: static storage: SRAM cells hold their data as long as the rail is up: no refresh cycles, unlike DRAM. The cost of keeping them is leakage through every cell's off transistors, which grows with temperature.
l2:l2.seq.no-refresh.01.source: textbook SRAM (GENERIC); the idle rail: docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md:110 and its table (67 °C 1.698 W, 82 °C 2.726 W)
